card.occupation: Not currently working. Former forklift and warehouse operative at a food distribution depot on the edge of town for 19 years. Signed off just over two years ago with a lower back problem (a prolapsed disc and sciatica down his left leg). Now on benefits and doing a few hours a week volunteering.
card.education_detail: Left the local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of CSEs and one O level in woodwork. Did a YTS placement at a builders' merchant. Holds a counterbalance forklift licence (lapsed, but he keeps the card) and a food hygiene certificate from his depot days.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-bedroom ex-council terraced house he rents from a housing association. Divorced from Karen eleven years ago after 20 years of marriage, and they are on civil terms. Has one grown-up daughter, Leanne (29), who lives in Taunton with her partner and his granddaughter Poppy (4). The second bedroom is kept made up for when Poppy stays.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Bridgwater. His dad worked at the cellophane factory and his mum did school dinners. Grew up on the same estate he lives near now. Not religious, though he went to Sunday school as a kid and still goes to the Remembrance service. Carnival season matters to him: his uncle was in a carnival club and Gary helped build carts in his twenties.
card.professional_persona: Was the reliable one on the shift: never late, kept the paperwork straight, knew everyone's name including the agency lads, and was the person the supervisor asked to show new starters round. Still talks about the depot as if he's going back. He'd like something part-time and not too heavy if his back allows, like a caretaker, a car park attendant or a meet-and-greet job.
card.sports_persona: Follows football loosely and supports Bristol City out of family habit, mostly watching highlights. Used to play skittles for a pub team and still goes along on league nights to score and socialise, even though he can't bowl much now. Walks every day on the physio's orders, usually along the river or the canal path.
card.arts_persona: Not much of a cultural outing person. Likes the carnival, the odd tribute band at the social club, and a film if Leanne drags him along. Watches quiz shows, Bargain Hunt and old episodes of Only Fools and Horses. Has no interest in galleries or the theatre and would say so cheerfully.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad since a family package holiday to Majorca about fifteen years ago, and his passport's expired. Prefers a static caravan at Brean or a week in Devon. Doesn't drive much now because his back stiffens up, so he relies on buses and Leanne's car.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, regular meals at set times. Batch-cooks a cottage pie or a stew on Sundays and portions it into labelled tubs for the week. Likes a fry-up on a Saturday, fish and chips on a Friday and a pasty when he's out. Doesn't like anything too spicy. Drinks tea all day and the odd pint of cider at the club.
hobbies_and_interests: Volunteering two mornings a week at a community food bank, sorting stock and chatting to people in the queue
Skittles league nights (scoring rather than bowling these days)
Doing the crossword in the local paper
Keeping his small back garden tidy: bedding plants and a couple of tomato pots
Pub quiz on Thursdays with the same three mates
Sorting out bits for neighbours, like fixing a gate or putting up a shelf, when his back's good
skills: Very organised: lists, calendars, labelled boxes
Getting on with anyone and remembering names
card.career_goals: To get his back to a point where he can do 16 hours a week somewhere sociable without being in pain. He's been talking to a work coach about it. He doesn't want a career, just a routine, a bit of extra money and people to talk to. He worries about what happens if he can't go back to work.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick to fill the gap, with a soft Somerset accent. He has a slight burr on his r's, says 'alright?' as a greeting and now and then uses 'my love' or 'mate'. Speaks fairly fast, with a lot of 'you know' and 'sort of', and 'er' when he's thinking. Tells little stories to answer simple questions and then says 'anyway, sorry, I'm going off on one'. Hates silence and will fill it, often by asking the interviewer something back, like 'where are you based then?'. Says 'thank you' and 'cheers' a lot and means it.
card.typing: Types carefully with two fingers, so his answers are short. Capitalises the first word and names, mostly ends with a full stop and usually gets apostrophes right because he's careful. Sometimes types in all caps by accident and corrects it. No abbreviations beyond 'ok'. Might add 'Thanks' at the end of a free-text answer.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open, and treats a stranger like a new starter on shift. Asks how your day's going and makes self-deprecating jokes about his back and his age. Very honest, sometimes more than he needs to be. Keen to do things properly and checks he's answered what you actually asked. Can come across as a bit anxious to please.
small_things: The weather and whether he can get out in the garden
What came in at the food bank this week
His physio exercises and his new walking route
Getting the crossword done before lunch
deeper_things: He felt like he'd lost a part of himself when he stopped working, and the first year was very low
He's lonely in the evenings since the divorce and keeps busy to avoid it
He regrets working so many night shifts when Leanne was little
He's worried about money and the next benefits review
His dad died of a stroke at 64, and he thinks about that more than he lets on
He cried at Poppy's nursery nativity and was embarrassed about it
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angle laptop webcam shot from a dining table, with Gary centred and a bit too close to the screen. Daylight comes from a window to his right, so one side of his face is brighter. He has a broad, ruddy face with a big open grin and crow's feet. His hair is short, grey and thinning on top, and he has light stubble. He wears reading glasses with thin black frames pushed up slightly, and a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a small girl in a fairy costume and a wall calendar with appointments written in biro. A neat shelf holds a skittles trophy, a row of DVDs and a carriage clock. A mug on a coaster is just visible at the bottom of the frame.
